thread.title: UPDATE: Facebook, Apple and Microsoft workers donate billions in political cash to the left

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: Facebook, Apple and Microsoft workers donate billions in political cash to the left
text:
By Shawn Langlois, MarketWatch
Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley employees are a corporate rarity with more Republican support than Democrat
Democrats may be outnumbered in Washington D.C.'s corridors of power these days, but when it comes to drawing political cash from Corporate America over the past decade, the blue team rules by a rather large margin.
With one big exception.
Cost-estimating website HowMuch.net crunched Federal Election Commission data (https://howmuch.net/articles/the-30-biggest-political-donors-on-the-fortune-500) from 250,000 of the country's biggest companies going back to 2007 to create this chart of the 30 most politically active companies in the Fortune 500.
Of note, these donations are from employees, not the companies themselves.
As you can see, financial giant Goldman Sachs (GS) tops the list by a wide margin, with its employees leaning just slightly toward Republican. Morgan Stanley (MS) is the only other company in the top 10 to put more money into GOP coffers than into the hands of the left.
Interestingly, Charles Schwab (SCHW) splits from its fellow banking institutions with 70% of its donations spent on Democratic candidates.
"Republicans received more than 50% of donations from only nine of the 30 companies, most of which tend to be grouped toward the bottom," HowMuch.net's Raul Amoros wrote. "Ultimately, it's fair to say that employees of these big companies have spent the bulk of their political cash on Democrats over the last decade."
Other big supporters of the left include Microsoft (MSFT) at 80% and Apple (AAPL) at 88%. Facebook (FB) leads the way at 91%.
Amoros also pointed out utilities like Comcast (CMCSA) and AT&T (T) have a vested interest in the net neutrality debate (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/washington-is-first-state-to-set-up-own-net-neutrality-requirement-in-rebuff-of-fcc-2018-03-06), while Boeing (BA) and Lockheed (LMT) rely on government contracts for business.
"In short, what's a couple billion dollars spent on a political campaign if it means the government will stay out of your way?" he said. "Political contributions might be one of the smartest investments some workers can make for their own job security."
-Shawn Langlois;
 1421ET
